headline: TOP SCORER: I
**CHEATED** WITH AI
cover.hook_pick_reason: The quote hook is clear in two seconds, names the confession and the AI, and slides 1 and 2 deliver it directly, framed as his self-report ('said he cheated') rather than a ruling. The proctors hook hides the exam and the AI, the 1 of 160 hook hides the AI angle, and the claim hook states as fact what is only a self-report. No reader-impact hook: the article reports one exam case and the agency's response, and states no effect on what ordinary readers pay, use or risk.
cover.image_prompt: Cinematic wide shot of a silent, empty national exam hall at night: rows of wooden desks with blank answer sheets, a single tiny glass lens catching a point of cold blue light on one desk, a smartphone lying face-up beside it glowing with soft abstract amber circuit patterns, long shadows from tall windows, shallow depth of field, moody teal and amber grading. No text, no letters, no logos, no people.

slides.title: A top scorer said he cheated
body: The top passer of Korea's 63rd **tax accountant exam**, a national licence test, said he cheated with a micro camera and generative AI. It is a self-report, and police have reportedly opened an investigation.

slides.title: Camera, AI, smartphone
body: He said he photographed the questions, sent them to AI and read the answers on a smartphone. He did not name the AI model or equipment, saying details could enable repeats. He will tell **investigators only**.

slides.title: One wrong out of 160
body: In April's first round he missed only **1 of 160 questions**, then scored high on the July second round and finished as the overall top passer. He said he used the same method on this year's first-round CPA exam, which he failed.

slides.title: Agency found no red flags
body: After doubts were raised, the Human Resources Development Service of Korea (HRDK), which runs the exam, checked with its proctors and found **nothing suspicious**.

slides.title: HRDK apologises, acts
body: On the 15th HRDK apologised. It will file a complaint for **obstruction of business**, seek to cancel his pass, and check other national exams.

slides.title: Ministry weighs suspension
body: The Ministry of Finance and Economy is **considering suspending** his pass. Police have reportedly opened an investigation after his self-report. The ministry is still considering.

facts.text: The top passer of Korea's 63rd tax accountant exam said he cheated with a micro camera and generative AI: he photographed questions, sent them to AI, and read the answers on a smartphone.
In the April first round he missed only 1 of 160 questions, and he then scored high on the July second round and finished as the overall top passer.
He said he used the same method on this year's first-round CPA exam, which he failed.
After doubts were raised, the Human Resources Development Service of Korea (HRDK), which runs the exam, checked with its exam proctors and found nothing suspicious.
On the 15th HRDK apologised, will file a complaint for obstruction of business, seek to cancel his pass, and check other national exams.
The Ministry of Finance and Economy is considering suspending the pass; police have reportedly opened an investigation after his self-report.
He did not disclose the AI model or equipment, saying details could enable repeats; he will tell investigators only.

caption:
Korea's tax accountant exam top scorer said he cheated with a micro camera and generative AI.

The exam is a national licence test run by the Human Resources Development Service of Korea (HRDK). The case is his self-report, which police have reportedly opened an investigation into. It is not a ruling.

→ He missed only 1 of 160 questions in the April first round, then scored high on the July second round and finished as the overall top passer
→ After doubts were raised, HRDK checked with its proctors and found nothing suspicious, then apologised and said it will seek to cancel his pass
→ The Ministry of Finance and Economy is considering suspending the pass

Can any exam stay cheat-proof when AI fits in a pocket?

Source: AI Times, "Top passer of tax accountant exam confesses to cheating with generative AI" (in Korean), Nov 15, 2026.
